title: Total influence decomposition
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, and let $f$ be real-valued on its outcome space. Its total influence equals $\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}} |S|\,\mathbb E_P[f_S^2]$, where $f_S$ is its $S$-component.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses
$f$ is real-valued on the outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Then $I(f)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}|S|\mathbb E_Pf_S^2$.
